# R07 Read-testing scrolls and every scroll prompt (A)

## Summary

- Eight unknown scrolls are worth investigating, but do not read-test all of them indiscriminately. First BUC-test them where possible, and avoid reading while blind, hallucinating, or confused. Current NetHackWiki guidance recommends preparing specifically for destroy armour, fire, enchant weapon, earth, genocide, and teleportation. The Wiki does not identify a specific game version for that advice. [NetHackWiki: Scroll](https://nethackwiki.com/wiki/Scroll?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- The 5.0 scroll-generation table gives identify a relative probability of 180, or 18% of the total scroll-generation weight. If eight scrolls were independent samples from that same table, the chance that at least one is identify would be \\(1-0.82^8 \approx 79.6\\%\\). Actual carried scrolls can come from different generation contexts, so treat that as a baseline, not a guarantee. [5.0 `objects.h`, scroll definitions](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/include/objects.h?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1138-L1185)
- Never read an unknown scroll while confused. For a human Valkyrie, confused genocide can kill the hero by genociding the human race; cursed or confused teleportation can cause a level teleport; and confused reading changes the effects of several other scrolls. [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_genocide()` and `do_genocide()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1631-L1645) [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_teleportation()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1907-L1922)
- Remove valuable armour before blind scroll testing. Ordinary destroy-armour reading can destroy a worn piece. Blessed destroy armour in 5.0 has a selection prompt when more than one piece is worn, but that is not a safe reason to test an unknown scroll while wearing valuable gear. [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_destroy_armor()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1293-L1320)
- Do not confuse “the scroll identified itself” with “the scroll had a useful effect.” Some scrolls only formally identify under particular conditions; for example, unknown cursed identify and confused identify identify themselves but do not open the inventory-identification operation. [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_identify()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1944-L1986)
- A non-cursed remove-curse scroll read while not confused can remove punishment. The chain is removed, but the iron ball remains on the floor. [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_remove_curse()` and `unpunish()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1408-L1521) [5.0 `read.c`, `unpunish()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2899-L2910)

### Decision table: every scroll type

“Read now?” assumes the bot has reached a safe place, is not blind, confused, or hallucinating, and has prepared its inventory. BUC known means the bot has established the item's BUC status independently, preferably by an altar test. A clue message is not always formal scroll identification.

| Scroll                               | Read now?                                                                                         | Recognition, prompts, and best answer                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Cursed and confused effects                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Identify                             | Yes, if not confused.                                                                             | Unknown usable identify normally says `This is an identify scroll.` and proceeds to item identification. Select the most valuable or dangerous unidentified item(s) in the inventory menu. If the scroll is unknown and cursed, or the hero is confused, it says `You identify this as an identify scroll.` and only identifies itself; there is no inventory-identification operation. [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_identify()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1944-L1986) [5.0 `invent.c`, `identify_pack()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/invent.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2561-L2595)                                                                                        | Cursed unknown identify only self-identifies. Confused identify also only self-identifies, regardless of BUC. Blessed identify can identify multiple items; uncursed identify usually identifies one, with a chance to identify more. [5.0 `read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1944-L1986)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Light                                | Yes, staged.                                                                                      | Normally lights the room; the room becoming illuminated is the recognition signal if the hero is not blind. No prompt. [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_light()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1649-L1684)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Cursed, unconfused reading darkens the room. Confused reading creates lights instead of lighting the room; the kind of light depends on BUC. [5.0 `read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1649-L1684)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Enchant weapon                       | Only after BUC-testing and protecting the weapon.                                                 | The wielded weapon is the target; no target-selection prompt. The weapon may glow or otherwise show the enchantment effect. Unwield a valuable highly enchanted long sword first; use a spare weapon only if you intend to enchant it. [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_enchant_weapon()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1540-L1587)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Cursed reading decreases the wielded weapon's enchantment. Confused non-cursed reading changes its erosion-proofing/repairs erosion instead of enchanting it; cursed confused reading removes erosion-proofing. [5.0 `read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1540-L1587)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Enchant armour                       | Only after BUC-testing and isolating a target.                                                    | No item-selection menu. `some_armor()` chooses the target using the worn pieces. Remove valuable competing armour and wear only the intended sacrificial or upgrade target. If no eligible armour is worn, it does not provide the expected enchantment. [5.0 `do_wear.c`, `some_armor()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/do_wear.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2493-L2515) [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_enchant_armor()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1051-L1070)                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Cursed reading decreases enchantment and curses the target; high enchantment can also trigger evaporation. | Remove curse                         | Yes, if not confused.                                                                             | Usually gives a helpful-feeling message, such as `You feel like someone is helping you.` No selection prompt. If already confused, the result depends on BUC: blessed can clear confusion, uncursed can extend it, and cursed sustains/causes it. [5.0 `read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1322-L1373)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

| Create monster                       | Not as a blind test. ### Important prompt details

A few prompt details deserve special handling in a bot:

- Identify: the identification UI is menu-style dependent. The source calls the inventory-identification routines; there is no safe universal literal item-menu key sequence to hard-code. Use the displayed item letters and select the highest-value unidentified item. [5.0 `invent.c`, `identify_pack()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/invent.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2561-L2595)
- Genocide: `none`/Escape is safe for the blessed class prompt and the known-uncursed species prompt. It is not safe as a universal response for a potentially cursed species prompt; cursed reverse genocide can select a random type when no type is given. [5.0 `read.c`, `do_class_genocide()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2495-L2553) [5.0 `read.c`, `do_genocide()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2808-L2853)
- Fire: never use Escape as a safety response to the explosion-position prompt. The fire routine does not treat unsuccessful position selection as a harmless cancellation; it can center the effect on the hero. [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_fire()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1750-L1815)
- Stinking cloud: Escape is a genuine cancellation at its position prompt. [5.0 `read.c`, `do_stinking_cloud()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2912-L2937)
- Blessed destroy armour: the 5.0 target-selection path is new relative to commonly repeated older advice. The source confirms the selector call, but its exact terminal prompt wording is UNVERIFIED for the NLE rendering. More importantly, Escape is not a safe substitute for selecting a sacrificial piece. [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_destroy_armor()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1293-L1320)
- Charging: the scroll opens a target selector after it is consumed. Escape can cancel the charge operation, but it does not return the scroll. [5.0 `read.c`, `seffect_charging()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1692-L1730)

## Bot rules

### Rule 1 — BUC-test before reading dangerous candidates

- Trigger = Inventory contains an unknown scroll and the hero is on an altar tile; hero is not blind or hallucinating.
- Action =
  1. Press `d`.
  2. Select the scroll's current inventory letter.
  3. If it is a stack, drop one item rather than the entire stack.
  4. Observe the altar flash.
  5. Record `black = cursed`, `amber = blessed`, `no flash = uncursed`.
  6. Pick the scroll back up with `,` and select it from the pickup list if necessary.
- Done when = The scroll's BUC state has been recorded and the scroll is back in inventory.
- If it fails = If there is no visible flash, or the hero is blind/hallucinating, mark BUC as unknown. Do not infer uncursed from an unreadable or ambiguous observation.
- Evidence = NetHackWiki's altar BUC-testing instructions; version not specified. [NetHackWiki: Altar](https://nethackwiki.com/wiki/Altar?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### Rule 2 — Prepare the room and equipment

- Trigger = The bot is about to read-test an unknown scroll.
- Action =
  1. Check status for confusion, blindness, and hallucination. Do not read-test while any is active.
  2. Move to a quiet, open place away from visible hostiles, peaceful monsters, and pets.
  3. Before a test that could be destroy armour, remove valuable armour. If armour must remain worn, leave only an inexpensive sacrificial piece.
  4. Before a test that could be enchant weapon, unwield the long sword if it is highly enchanted or otherwise valuable.
  5. Before a possible fire scroll, put flammable inventory (especially scrolls, spellbooks, and potions) into a container or move it away from the blast area.
  6. Before a possible earth scroll, wear a hard helmet and avoid Sokoban, boulder-trap areas, and locations where falling boulders can trap a pet.
- Done when = The hero is not confused/blind/hallucinating, valuable equipment is protected, and the nearby area is clear.
- If it fails = Defer read-testing. Keep the scroll unidentified rather than risk losing a valuable item or the run.
- Evidence = NetHackWiki's scroll-identification precautions; current Wiki version unspecified. [NetHackWiki: Scroll](https://nethackwiki.com/wiki/Scroll?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### Rule 3 — Read a low-risk candidate

- Trigger = The scroll has a known or acceptably safe BUC state, the hero is not confused/blind/hallucinating, and the room is prepared.
- Action =
  1. Press `r`.
  2. Enter the scroll's current inventory letter.
  3. Read the resulting message.
  4. If an item-selection prompt appears, select only a known appropriate target.
  5. If a charge selector appears and no item should be charged, press Escape.
  6. If a stinking-cloud position prompt appears and the bot does not want to create a cloud, press Escape.
- Done when = The scroll's identity has been added to the bot's item-knowledge state, or the scroll has been recorded as consumed without a definitive identification.
- If it fails = Do not repeat a test just because the message was generic. Record the exact text and mark the scroll unresolved.
- Evidence = 5.0 `src/read.c::doread()` and the individual `seffect_*()` functions. [5.0 `read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L588-L608)

### Rule 4 — Handle blessed destroy-armour selection

- Trigger = The bot has deliberately read a known blessed destroy-armour scroll and the terminal opens the destroy-armour item selector.
- Action =
  1. Inspect the displayed eligible armour.
  2. Select the least valuable sacrificial item by its current inventory letter.
  3. Do not press Escape as an assumed cancellation.
- Done when = The selected item is destroyed and the scroll's effect is complete.
- If it fails = If no expendable armour is available, do not initiate this scroll's use. The safe action is to keep it for later.
- Evidence = 5.0 `src/read.c::seffect_destroy_armor()` calls `getobj("destroy", ...)` for blessed reading when more than one armour piece is worn; the default target remains active if no replacement is selected. [5.0 `read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1293-L1320)

### Rule 5 — Handle genocide prompts conservatively

- Trigger = The terminal reports `You have found a scroll of genocide!` and then opens a class or species prompt.
- Action =
  - If the prompt is `What class of monsters do you want to genocide?`, enter `none` and press Enter, or press Escape.
  - If the prompt is `What type of monster do you want to genocide?` and the bot has independently established that the scroll is uncursed, enter `none` and press Enter, or press Escape.
  - If the species prompt appears and the scroll might be cursed, do not use `none` or Escape as a supposed safe cancellation. The safest policy is to avoid reading until BUC is known.
- Done when = The prompt closes without an unintended genocide or reverse-genocide result.
- If it fails = If the hero is confused and the scroll was non-blessed, treat the run as in immediate danger: the human hero can be genocided. Do not proceed with normal exploration assumptions.
- Evidence = 5.0 `src/read.c::do_class_genocide()` and `do_genocide()`. [5.0 `read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2495-L2553) [5.0 `read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2686-L2690)

### Rule 6 — Handle position prompts

- Trigger = A scroll produces a position prompt such as `Where do you want to center the stinking cloud?`, `Where do you want to center the explosion?`, or `Where do you want to be teleported?`.
- Action =
  - Stinking cloud: press Escape to cancel safely, or choose a valid square away from the hero and peaceful creatures.
  - Fire: do not press Escape. Only proceed if a valid visible square is available away from the hero and vulnerable inventory.
  - Ordinary controlled teleport: choose a known-safe legal destination; Escape cancels the ordinary position choice when the hero is not confused.
- Done when = The effect has been placed at the intended square or safely cancelled where cancellation is supported.
- If it fails = If the bot cannot distinguish which prompt is active, do not send a generic Escape response. Classify the prompt first; fire's failure path can center the explosion on the hero.
- Evidence = 5.0 `src/read.c::seffect_fire()`, `do_stinking_cloud()`, and 5.0 `src/teleport.c::scrolltele()`. [Fire](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1750-L1815) [Stinking cloud](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2912-L2937) [Teleport](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/teleport.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1097-L1151)

### Rule 7 — Remove punishment

- Trigger = The message `You are being punished for your misbehavior!` appears, or the status/inventory observations indicate the hero is punished and has a ball and chain.
- Action =
  1. Check inventory for a known blessed or uncursed scroll of remove curse.
  2. Confirm the hero is not confused.
  3. Press `r`.
  4. Select the known remove-curse scroll's inventory letter.
  5. After the chain disappears, inspect the floor for the iron ball.
  6. Pick up the ball only if the bot deliberately wants to carry it; otherwise leave it in a safe location.
- Done when = The punished state and chain are gone. The loose ball has been accounted for.
- If it fails = If the scroll is cursed or the hero is confused, do not expect punishment to be removed. Avoid repeatedly reading remove-curse scrolls in those states.
- Evidence = `seffect_remove_curse()` only calls `unpunish()` for the non-confused beneficial path; `unpunish()` removes the chain but leaves the ball. [5.0 `read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1408-L1521) [5.0 `read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2899-L2910)

## Risks and exceptions

1\. Do not assume every readable scroll identifies itself with a unique line. Some effects provide an indirect clue, some identify only when an effect is actually observed, and some require particular conditions. The bot should preserve the full message history and distinguish `identified`, `probable`, and `unresolved` states. [5.0 `src/read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

2\. The identify percentage is not necessarily the probability for every carried scroll. The 18% figure is the relative probability in the scroll-generation table. Monster equipment, special-level generation, shops, and other sources can bias the composition of the bot's inventory. [5.0 `include/objects.h`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/include/objects.h?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1138-L1185) [NetHackWiki: Scroll](https://nethackwiki.com/wiki/Scroll?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

3\. Confusion is an especially dangerous read-testing condition. It changes the effects of identify, enchant weapon, enchant armour, remove curse, scare monster, create monster, genocide, teleportation, fire, earth, and punishment. Even when an individual confused effect is harmless, it is not a reliable way to identify the scroll. [5.0 `src/read.c`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

4\. The fire scroll is an inventory hazard, not just an HP hazard. Its explosion can destroy vulnerable carried objects. The NetHackWiki preparation advice to protect scrolls, spellbooks, and potions before reading is particularly important for a bot carrying several unidentified scrolls. [NetHackWiki: Scroll](https://nethackwiki.com/wiki/Scroll?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [5.0 `read.c::seffect_fire()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1750-L1815)

5\. The earth scroll is not a harmless way to learn a type. A boulder can injure or trap the hero; even the blessed effect can produce obstructing boulders. The Wiki's recommendations to wear a hard helmet and avoid Sokoban and boulder-trap locations are sensible, but its page does not state a specific game version. [NetHackWiki: Scroll](https://nethackwiki.com/wiki/Scroll?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [5.0 `read.c::seffect_earth()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1817-L1867)

6\. Punishment impairs movement. The ball and chain are a real burden; NetHackWiki describes the movement and carrying complications, but exact behavior should be checked against the 5.0.0 source before turning every older Wiki detail into a hard-coded rule. [NetHackWiki: Punishment](https://nethackwiki.com/wiki/Punishment?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [5.0 `read.c::punish()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2855-L2897)

7\. Removing punishment does not destroy the ball. The source clears the chain and the worn-ball state but leaves the ball as an object. The bot must not assume the iron ball has vanished with the punishment status. [5.0 `read.c::unpunish()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L2899-L2910)

8\. Do not use the blessed destroy-armour selector as a safety net for an unknown scroll. The blessed prompt is conditional on more than one armour piece being worn; an uncursed or cursed destroy-armour read does not offer the same protective selection opportunity. [5.0 `read.c::seffect_destroy_armor()`](https://github.com/NetHack/NetHack/blob/NetHack-5.0.0_Released/src/read.c?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1293-L1320)

## Open questions

- Exact NLE prompt rendering: The source confirms the selector operations (`getobj("charge")`, `getobj("destroy")`, and the genocide prompts), but the precise rendered prompt text and menu behavior can depend on the NLE interface configuration. The literal visible wording for the destroy-armour and charging item selectors is UNVERIFIED for this NLE build.
- Exact NLE position-selection keys: The game source confirms when `getpos` is called and whether Escape cancels, but the precise cursor movement keys depend on the configured keymap. Their mapping is UNVERIFIED until tested in the bot's actual NLE build.
- Beginner hint behavior: Current NetHackWiki describes a beginner hint mechanism, but whether the same hint gate is active in the 5.0.0 release is UNVERIFIED. Do not rely on it to protect the bot from a dangerous unknown scroll.
- Mail scroll: Whether mail support is compiled into this NLE 5.0 build is UNVERIFIED.
- Punishment alternatives: The reliable source-verified removal path above is a known non-cursed remove-curse scroll while not confused. Other proposed removal methods should be separately checked against the exact 5.0.0 source before being implemented as guaranteed escape rules.
